skill.name: set-up-lightspeed-google-ads-customer-match
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up six Google Ads Customer Match audiences from paid orders in Lightspeed eCom (C-Series). Check tracking and consent prerequisites, verify list creation, and choose how to use the lists in Google Ads.
skill.summary: Set up and verify Google Ads Customer Match lists for Lightspeed eCom with Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most flags are Markdown notation, documentation links, or authorized setup checks, not shell substitution or host reconnaissance. The workflow does invoke a remote interface, read order records, and advertise an unpinned installer. The review found credential, setup scope, browser handoff, and privacy disclosure gaps, but no evidence of audit-directed prompt injection or covert exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The CLI credential exception conflicts with app-only credential entry.
remediation.suggestion: Remove chat and command-line credential collection. Direct the merchant to the verified Product Metrics app for secret entry and remove unrelated credential exceptions.

remediation.issue: Missing tracking can trigger a broader integration setup.
remediation.suggestion: Stop after reporting missing prerequisites. Obtain separate approval for Google-only tracking setup and name the workspace, client account, data destinations, and requested permissions.

remediation.issue: The hashing description contradicts the stated address payload.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the Data Manager payload and state exactly which fields are hashed and which fields are sent unhashed before asking users to enable list syncing.

remediation.issue: Browser handoff trusts a returned URL without checking its destination.
remediation.suggestion: Validate HTTPS and the expected provider origin before showing an authorization link. Tell the user the expected destination and requested access.

remediation.issue: Order lookup can retrieve more detail than the setup check needs.
remediation.suggestion: Use a limited classification response for the approved storefront. Do not include order identifiers, contact details, or margins in the setup report.

remediation.issue: The documented install command does not pin the runner or skill source.
remediation.suggestion: Document a reviewed runner version and immutable skill revision. Keep installation outside the normal setup workflow and require explicit approval.

remediation.issue: The remote fallback exposes a generic API execution interface.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only the Product Metrics operations needed for Customer Match. Confirm the workspace and property before any call that changes state.

semantic_findings.title: Credential handling permits secrets outside the secure form
semantic_findings.description: The agent rules allow collecting Lightspeed API credentials from the user and passing them to a command. The Lightspeed guide instead requires app entry and says to keep secrets out of chat. Agent inputs or tool logs can retain credentials even if the final answer omits them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception and direct command handoff are explicit. The same key grants customer and order reads plus settings and tracking writes.

semantic_findings.title: Customer Match workflow can expand into broader tracking setup
semantic_findings.description: Missing Google Ads tracking triggers setup rather than a status report or separate approval. The fallback reference also lists Meta and ChatGPT Ads and describes ongoing paid-order reporting. Following the full checklist can exceed a Google Customer Match request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scope expansion and channel list are explicit. Third-party approvals still require user action, and the instructions do not show that unrelated channels are connected automatically.

semantic_findings.title: Customer data disclosure contradicts the hashing statement
semantic_findings.description: The payload table lists unhashed country and postcode when address data is complete. The next paragraph says everything is hashed. A merchant relying on that assurance could enable ongoing uploads without understanding what Google receives.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The adjacent statements directly contradict each other. The packaged documentation does not verify the actual runtime payload.

semantic_findings.title: Browser authorization handoff lacks destination validation
semantic_findings.description: The agent is told to relay a URL returned by the service without checking the expected provider origin. A compromised or malformed response could send the user to an unexpected sign-in or consent page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly delegates opening the returned URL to the user but shows no origin check. No malicious redirect or runtime compromise was observed.

content.user_title: Set Up Lightspeed Customer Match in Google Ads
content.value_statement: Lightspeed merchants need current audiences to distinguish existing buyers from new prospects. This skill guides Product Metrics setup for six Google Ads lists that update from eligible paid orders.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status and identify missing prerequisites for the selected store and Google Ads account.
Check whether a paid test order was classified as a new or returning customer.
Guide configuration of the supported consent banner and identify where the merchant accepts Customer Match terms.
Guide creation of six Customer Match lists and identify any missing lists in Product Metrics.
Explain how All customers, Lapsed customers, and High-value customers can support different campaign goals.
limitations: The documented setup requires Lightspeed eCom (C-Series), Product Metrics Pro, a proxied Cloudflare domain, and working Google Ads tracking with Merchant Center.
Customers are not added from historical orders alone. They become eligible after their next paid order once the lists exist.
List creation does not change campaigns or bidding settings. Google Ads actions and approvals remain with the account user.
The bundled files are instructions. Live checks require authorized access through the Product Metrics CLI or MCP interface, or user verification in the app.

use_cases.title: Check readiness before creating lists
use_cases.description: Identify which Lightspeed, Google Ads, consent, and account steps are complete before enabling any list sync.

use_cases.title: Separate acquisition from existing customers
use_cases.description: Find the All customers list and verify that it has members before considering it as a campaign exclusion.

use_cases.title: Plan a lapsed customer audience
use_cases.description: Check how the Lapsed customers list fills and learn why it may not contain historical buyers immediately.

prompt_templates.title: List the setup requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Tell me what my Lightspeed store and Google Ads account need before I can create Customer Match lists. Do not connect anything.

prompt_templates.title: Check whether my setup is ready
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Customer Match readiness for my approved Product Metrics workspace and Google Ads account. Report missing steps without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Verify consent and a test order
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my paid test order was classified as new or returning. Report only the classification and what I must verify in my consent settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Applied: Validate the store before creating lists.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the list rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare All customers, Lapsed customers, and High-value customers for my Google Ads goals. Identify the checks before I use them. Do not modify campaigns.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Plan audience use after setup.

output_examples.input: What is blocking Customer Match for this store?
output: Lightspeed is active and the Google Ads client account is connected.
Accept the Customer Match terms in Google Ads before creating the lists.
I did not change the setup.

output_examples.input: The six lists exist. Why are they still empty?
output_examples.output: Past orders do not fill the lists automatically. Check for a paid order placed after list creation with both required advertising consent choices.

best_practices: Confirm the Lightspeed store, Product Metrics property, and Google Ads client account before approving changes.
Enter credentials only in the verified Product Metrics app and review each provider approval before granting access.
Check that the actual consent banner is configured, verify a paid test order, and confirm that the lists show members before using them.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API credentials or customer contact details into chat.
Do not enable tracking for other advertising channels as part of a Google Customer Match request.
Do not treat an empty or newly created list as a complete record of existing customers.

faq.question: Which Lightspeed stores are supported?
faq.answer: The documented setup supports Lightspeed eCom (C-Series) on the Europe and United States clusters.

faq.question: Which consent is required to add a customer?
faq.answer: The customer must allow both ad user data and ad personalization. Supported banners are OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, and Osano.

faq.question: Are existing customers added immediately?
faq.answer: No. Customers become eligible after their next paid order once the lists exist, subject to the required consent.

faq.question: What customer data goes to Google?
faq.answer: The payload table lists hashed email, phone, and names, plus unhashed country and postcode when the address fields are complete. Confirm this with Product Metrics before enabling sync.

faq.question: Who accepts the Customer Match terms?
faq.answer: A user who can manage the Google Ads client account accepts the terms directly in Google Ads.

faq.question: Does setup change my campaigns?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics creates and updates the lists. You choose whether to use them for exclusions, retention campaigns, or Performance Max audience signals.
